name: subselect_unpaged_ordered
comment: An unpaged subquery with orderings: SQLite and PostgreSQL render them as given; where paging requires ORDER BY (SQL Server) an ORDER BY without paging is illegal inside a subquery (error 1033), so the renderer omits an unpaged subquery's orderings there — membership is order-insensitive, the rows are the same. A paged subquery keeps them (subselect_membership.json).

sqlite.sql: select id, user_id, status, amount, version, note, created_at, updated_at from transactions where user_id in (select id from users where name = @c0 order by name) order by id

sqlserver.sql: select [id], [user_id], [status], [amount], [version], [note], [created_at], [updated_at] from [transactions] where [user_id] in (select [id] from [users] where [name] = @c0) order by [id]

postgres.sql: select "id", "user_id", "status", "amount", "version", "note", "created_at", "updated_at" from "transactions" where "user_id" in (select "id" from "users" where "name" = @c0 order by "name") order by "id"
